questions.cardText:
[Earth Science] What is the difference between lava and magma?
A. Magma contains more gas and is less viscous than lava
B. There is no difference
C. Whether they are found inside the Earth or not
Answer: C. Magma and lava are essentially the same substance — molten rock — but they are called different names based on their location. Magma is the term used when this molten rock is beneath the Earth’s surface. When magma erupts from a volcano and flows over the land or seabed, it’s known as lava.
questions.de: Geschmolzenes Gestein unter der Erdoberfläche heißt Magma – wie nennt man es, sobald es an die Oberfläche ausbricht?
questions.en: Molten rock beneath the Earth's surface is magma — what is it called once it erupts onto the surface?

timeline.labelEn: Francesco Serao's account of the Vesuvius eruption is an early use of 'lava' for erupted molten rock
timeline.labelDe: Francesco Seraos Bericht über den Ausbruch des Vesuvs ist eine frühe Verwendung von „Lava“ für ausgetretenes geschmolzenes Gestein

questions.notes: Confirmed: 'Lava is magma that has been expelled from the interior … onto its surface' (Wikipedia). Strictly, magma also holds crystals and dissolved gas that escape on eruption, so 'the same substance' is a simplification.

questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] What is the term for a system of millions or billions of stars, together with gas and dust, held together by gravitational attraction?
A. Galaxy B. Solar System C. Universe
Answer: A.
questions.de: Wie nennt man ein System aus Millionen oder Milliarden Sternen samt Gas und Staub, das durch die Schwerkraft zusammengehalten wird?
questions.en: What is the term for a system of millions or billions of stars, together with gas and dust, held together by gravitational attraction?
